每次 commit 后立刻更新 tip 这是我要改的第二点——不要等到 session 结束： ```bash git update-ref --create-reflog \ -m "session $SESSION_ID: $MSG" \ refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip HEAD ``` 两个好处。一是崩溃安全：agent 中途挂了、或者用户 `reset --hard` 了，对象从第一个 commit 起就被 ref 锚定，`gc` 碰不到。二是 **`--create-reflog` 让 tip 的 reflog 自动变成 session 日志**： ```bash git reflog show refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip ``` `refs/agent/` 不在默认开 reflog 的命名空间里（只有 heads/remotes/notes/HEAD 是），所以 `--create-reflog` 必须显式加。加上之后你白得一份带时间戳的、按序的 session 进展记录，不用自己写日志文件。 ## 需要原子性时 多个 ref 一起改，用 `update-ref --stdin`： ```bash git update-ref --stdin < ` 带旧值就是 compare-and-swap，并发下不会覆盖别人的写入。 ## 查询和清理 ```bash # 这个 session 干了什么 git log refs/agent/session/$ID/base..refs/agent/session/$ID/tip # 列所有 session git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:lstrip=3) %(objectname:short)' \ 'refs/agent/session/*/tip' # 从 trailer 反查（ref 丢了或过时了的时候） git log --all --format='%H %(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' \ | grep " $ID$" # 过期清理：ref 是派生数据，删了不丢信息 git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/agent/session/*' \ | xargs -n1 git update-ref -d ``` ## 一个容易踩的坑 `refs/agent/session//base` 和 `refs/agent/session/` 在 files 后端下不能共存——一个是目录一个是文件。所以要么统一用 `/base` `/tip` 两个子 ref（我上面这样），要么统一只用一个。别混着来，否则第一个 session 好好的，第二个 session 换了命名方式就直接报错。这也正好是 reftable 顺带解决掉的那类问题。 # Commit message trailer Before 2026.8.31 形如 Co-authored-by: claude code/claude-opus-5/b47c8939-8ae6-4c1b-b9b2-f89c387b3e77 ## 它能工作，但你把两件事压进了一个字段 `Co-authored-by` 是一个语义明确的身份字段：`Name `。你在 name 的位置塞了 `工具/模型/session-id` 三段位置编码的数据。git 不会报错——name 就是 `<` 之前的自由文本——但这有几个实际代价。 **1. shortlog 会被打爆。** ```bash git shortlog -s --group=trailer:Co-authored-by ``` 按 trailer 分组时，每个 session 都是一个不同的「人」。跑几百个 session 之后这个输出就没法看了。mailmap 也救不了，你得给每个 session 写一行。 **2. GitHub 侧的显示。** 它按 email 匹配账号，所有 session 的 email 相同，所以会折叠成一个 co-author，但显示名就是那串 UUID。PR 页面上不太好看。 **3. 位置编码不可扩展。** 现在是三段，哪天想加个 `Agent-Version` 或者某段可选，所有解析代码一起改。而且分隔符 `/` 出现在模型名里就直接歧义了。 **4. 查询要额外剥一层。** 拿 session id 得先取 trailer，再 split： ```bash git log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly)' \ | awk -F'[/ ]' '{print $1, $4}' ``` 对比一个独立 trailer 可以直接 `%(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)` 拿到干净的值。 ## 拆开 ``` Co-authored-by: Claude Agent-Tool: claude-code Agent-Model: claude-opus-5 Agent-Session-Id: b47c8939-8ae6-4c1b-b9b2-f89c387b3e77 ``` ```bash git commit -m "$MSG" \ --trailer "Co-authored-by: Claude " \ --trailer "Agent-Tool: claude-code" \ --trailer "Agent-Model: claude-opus-5" \ --trailer "Agent-Session-Id: $SESSION_ID" ``` `Co-authored-by` 回归它的本职——GitHub 归因、shortlog 里就是一个固定的 co-author。元数据各占一个 key，各自独立可查、可增可减。多 trailer 是完全惯用的写法，squash merge 时也会被保留合并。 这样前面那套查询就直接能用了： ```bash git log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' \ refs/agent/session/$ID/base..refs/agent/session/$ID/tip \ | awk -v id="$ID" '$2 == id { print $1 }' ``` ## 已有历史不用改写 新旧两种格式可以共存。写个函数同时认： ```bash session_of() { local sha=$1 v v=$(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' "$sha") [ -n "$v" ] && { echo "$v"; return; } # 回退到旧的三段式 git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly)' "$sha" \ | sed -n 's#.*/\([0-9a-f-]\{36\}\) <.*#\1#p' } ``` 跑一遍就能把旧 commit 的 session ref 重建出来，不需要 rebase。 ## 另外 有些项目对 AI co-author trailer 有明确态度——Linux 内核、以及一部分要求 DCO sign-off 的项目，会把 `Co-authored-by` 当作真实的作者声明来处理，塞机器身份进去可能被要求改掉。这跟你要不要拆字段无关，但如果你会往外部仓库推，值得先确认对方的 contributing 规则。拆开之后正好也方便——需要时去掉 `Co-authored-by` 那一行，`Agent-*` 的元数据完全不受影响。 session 开始 从agent（claude code等）获得SESSION_ID ```bash BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD) # unborn branch 会失败，先判一下 git update-ref --create-reflog \ -m "session $SESSION_ID start" \ refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/base "$BASE" ``` 不要 `checkout -b`。base SHA 已经完整记录了起点，建分支只是多了个要清理的东西。 **如果确实需要隔离**（不想动用户正在编辑的文件，或让两个 session 真的在不同的历史上），用 worktree 而不是切分支： ```bash git worktree add --detach /tmp/agent-$SESSION_ID "$BASE" cd /tmp/agent-$SESSION_ID ``` 这样 agent 有独立的工作区和独立的 HEAD，用户那边完全无感。`--detach` 是刻意的——不建分支名，省掉命名冲突和清理。结束后 `git worktree remove`，commit 对象留在共享的 object store 里，靠你的 ref 锚定。 ## 每次 commit ```bash git commit -m "$MSG" --trailer "Agent-Session-Id: $SESSION_ID" ``` `--trailer` 需要 git 2.32+，老版本用 `git interpret-trailers --trailer ... | git commit -F -`。 关键点是**每次都显式传**，不要依赖 hook 或 `commit.template`。显式参数不依赖任何环境状态，也就不需要「确保当前分支」这种检查。 如果要防止别人的 commit 混进来： ```bash NEW=$(git rev-parse HEAD) PARENT=$(git rev-parse HEAD^) [ "$PARENT" = "$EXPECTED" ] || echo "有人在中间插了 commit" EXPECTED=$NEW ``` 比对 SHA 比比对分支名可靠得多。 ## 每次 commit 后立刻更新 tip 这是我要改的第二点——不要等到 session 结束： ```bash git update-ref --create-reflog \ -m "session $SESSION_ID: $MSG" \ refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip HEAD ``` 两个好处。一是崩溃安全：agent 中途挂了、或者用户 `reset --hard` 了，对象从第一个 commit 起就被 ref 锚定，`gc` 碰不到。二是 **`--create-reflog` 让 tip 的 reflog 自动变成 session 日志**： ```bash git reflog show refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip ``` `refs/agent/` 不在默认开 reflog 的命名空间里（只有 heads/remotes/notes/HEAD 是），所以 `--create-reflog` 必须显式加。加上之后你白得一份带时间戳的、按序的 session 进展记录，不用自己写日志文件。 ## 需要原子性时 多个 ref 一起改，用 `update-ref --stdin`： ```bash git update-ref --stdin < ` 带旧值就是 compare-and-swap，并发下不会覆盖别人的写入。 ## 查询和清理 ```bash # 这个 session 干了什么 git log refs/agent/session/$ID/base..refs/agent/session/$ID/tip # 列所有 session git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:lstrip=3) %(objectname:short)' \ 'refs/agent/session/*/tip' # 从 trailer 反查（ref 丢了或过时了的时候） git log --all --format='%H %(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' \ | grep " $ID$" # 过期清理：ref 是派生数据，删了不丢信息 git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/agent/session/*' \ | xargs -n1 git update-ref -d ``` ## 一个容易踩的坑 `refs/agent/session//base` 和 `refs/agent/session/` 在 files 后端下不能共存——一个是目录一个是文件。所以要么统一用 `/base` `/tip` 两个子 ref（我上面这样），要么统一只用一个。别混着来，否则第一个 session 好好的，第二个 session 换了命名方式就直接报错。这也正好是 reftable 顺带解决掉的那类问题。 # Commit message trailer Before 2026.8.31 形如 Co-authored-by: claude code/claude-opus-5/b47c8939-8ae6-4c1b-b9b2-f89c387b3e77 ## GitHub 侧的显示。** 它按 email 匹配账号，所有 session 的 email 相同，所以会折叠成一个 co-author，但显示名就是那串 UUID。PR 页面上不太好看。 **3. 位置编码不可扩展。** 现在是三段，哪天想加个 `Agent-Version` 或者某段可选，所有解析代码一起改。而且分隔符 `/` 出现在模型名里就直接歧义了。 **4. 查询要额外剥一层。** `checkout -b` 解决的是「隔离」，但它是最粗糙的那种隔离——它动了用户的工作区和 HEAD。而「commit 时确保当前分支」是在用环境状态当契约，这在 agent 场景下很脆：用户可能在另一个终端切了分支，或者你自己的某个工具调用里跑了 `checkout`。

正确的不变量不是「我在哪个分支上」，而是**「上一个 commit 是不是我预期的那个 SHA」**。

## session 开始

从agent（claude code等）获得SESSION_ID

```bash
BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)   # unborn branch 会失败，先判一下

git update-ref --create-reflog \
    -m "session $SESSION_ID start" \
    refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/base "$BASE"
```

不要 `checkout -b`。base SHA 已经完整记录了起点，建分支只是多了个要清理的东西。

**如果确实需要隔离**（不想动用户正在编辑的文件，或让两个 session 真的在不同的历史上），用 worktree 而不是切分支：

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/agent-$SESSION_ID "$BASE"
cd /tmp/agent-$SESSION_ID
```

这样 agent 有独立的工作区和独立的 HEAD，用户那边完全无感。`--detach` 是刻意的——不建分支名，省掉命名冲突和清理。结束后 `git worktree remove`，commit 对象留在共享的 object store 里，靠你的 ref 锚定。

## 每次 commit

```bash
git commit -m "$MSG" --trailer "Agent-Session-Id: $SESSION_ID"
```

`--trailer` 需要 git 2.32+，老版本用 `git interpret-trailers --trailer ... | git commit -F -`。

关键点是**每次都显式传**，不要依赖 hook 或 `commit.template`。显式参数不依赖任何环境状态，也就不需要「确保当前分支」这种检查。

如果要防止别人的 commit 混进来：

```bash
NEW=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
PARENT=$(git rev-parse HEAD^)
[ "$PARENT" = "$EXPECTED" ] || echo "有人在中间插了 commit"
EXPECTED=$NEW
```

比对 SHA 比比对分支名可靠得多。

`checkout -b` 解决的是「隔离」，但它是最粗糙的那种隔离——它动了用户的工作区和 HEAD。而「commit 时确保当前分支」是在用环境状态当契约，这在 agent 场景下很脆：用户可能在另一个终端切了分支，或者你自己的某个工具调用里跑了 `checkout`。

正确的不变量不是「我在哪个分支上」，而是**「上一个 commit 是不是我预期的那个 SHA」**。

## session 开始

从agent（claude code等）获得SESSION_ID

```bash
BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)   # unborn branch 会失败，先判一下

git update-ref --create-reflog \
    -m "session $SESSION_ID start" \
    refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/base "$BASE"
```

不要 `checkout -b`。base SHA 已经完整记录了起点，建分支只是多了个要清理的东西。

**如果确实需要隔离**（不想动用户正在编辑的文件，或让两个 session 真的在不同的历史上），用 worktree 而不是切分支：

```bash
git worktree add --detach /tmp/agent-$SESSION_ID "$BASE"
cd /tmp/agent-$SESSION_ID
```

这样 agent 有独立的工作区和独立的 HEAD，用户那边完全无感。`--detach` 是刻意的——不建分支名，省掉命名冲突和清理。结束后 `git worktree remove`，commit 对象留在共享的 object store 里，靠你的 ref 锚定。

## 每次 commit

```bash
git commit -m "$MSG" --trailer "Agent-Session-Id: $SESSION_ID"
```

`--trailer` 需要 git 2.32+，老版本用 `git interpret-trailers --trailer ... | git commit -F -`。

关键点是**每次都显式传**，不要依赖 hook 或 `commit.template`。显式参数不依赖任何环境状态，也就不需要「确保当前分支」这种检查。

如果要防止别人的 commit 混进来：

```bash
NEW=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
PARENT=$(git rev-parse HEAD^)
[ "$PARENT" = "$EXPECTED" ] || echo "有人在中间插了 commit"
EXPECTED=$NEW
```

比对 SHA 比比对分支名可靠得多。

## 每次 commit 后立刻更新 tip

这是我要改的第二点——不要等到 session 结束：

```bash
git update-ref --create-reflog \
    -m "session $SESSION_ID: $MSG" \
    refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip HEAD
```

两个好处。一是崩溃安全：agent 中途挂了、或者用户 `reset --hard` 了，对象从第一个 commit 起就被 ref 锚定，`gc` 碰不到。二是 **`--create-reflog` 让 tip 的 reflog 自动变成 session 日志**：

```bash
git reflog show refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip
```

`refs/agent/` 不在默认开 reflog 的命名空间里（只有 heads/remotes/notes/HEAD 是），所以 `--create-reflog` 必须显式加。加上之后你白得一份带时间戳的、按序的 session 进展记录，不用自己写日志文件。

## 需要原子性时

多个 ref 一起改，用 `update-ref --stdin`：

```bash
git update-ref --stdin <<EOF
start
update refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/tip $NEW $OLD
create refs/agent/session/$SESSION_ID/base $BASE
prepare
commit
EOF
```

`update <ref> <new> <old>` 带旧值就是 compare-and-swap，并发下不会覆盖别人的写入。

## 查询和清理

```bash
# 这个 session 干了什么
git log refs/agent/session/$ID/base..refs/agent/session/$ID/tip

# 列所有 session
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:lstrip=3) %(objectname:short)' \
    'refs/agent/session/*/tip'

# 从 trailer 反查（ref 丢了或过时了的时候）
git log --all --format='%H %(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' \
  | grep " $ID$"

  | xargs -n1 git update-ref -d
```

## 一个容易踩的坑

`refs/agent/session/<id>/base` 和 `refs/agent/session/<id>` 在 files 后端下不能共存——一个是目录一个是文件。所以要么统一用 `/base` `/tip` 两个子 ref（我上面这样），要么统一只用一个。别混着来，否则第一个 session 好好的，第二个 session 换了命名方式就直接报错。这也正好是 reftable 顺带解决掉的那类问题。

# Commit message trailer

Before 2026.8.31 形如 Co-authored-by: claude code/claude-opus-5/b47c8939-8ae6-4c1b-b9b2-f89c387b3e77 <noreply@anthropic.com>

## 它能工作，但你把两件事压进了一个字段

`Co-authored-by` 是一个语义明确的身份字段：`Name <email>`。你在 name 的位置塞了 `工具/模型/session-id` 三段位置编码的数据。git 不会报错——name 就是 `<` 之前的自由文本——但这有几个实际代价。

**1. shortlog 会被打爆。**

```bash
git shortlog -s --group=trailer:Co-authored-by
```

按 trailer 分组时，每个 session 都是一个不同的「人」。跑几百个 session 之后这个输出就没法看了。mailmap 也救不了，你得给每个 session 写一行。

**2. GitHub 侧的显示。** 它按 email 匹配账号，所有 session 的 email 相同，所以会折叠成一个 co-author，但显示名就是那串 UUID。PR 页面上不太好看。

**3. 位置编码不可扩展。** 现在是三段，哪天想加个 `Agent-Version` 或者某段可选，所有解析代码一起改。而且分隔符 `/` 出现在模型名里就直接歧义了。

**4. 查询要额外剥一层。** 拿 session id 得先取 trailer，再 split：

```bash
git log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly)' \
  | awk -F'[/ ]' '{print $1, $4}'
```

对比一个独立 trailer 可以直接 `%(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)` 拿到干净的值。

## 拆开

```
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Agent-Tool: claude-code
Agent-Model: claude-opus-5
Agent-Session-Id: b47c8939-8ae6-4c1b-b9b2-f89c387b3e77
```

```bash
git commit -m "$MSG" \
  --trailer "Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>" \
  --trailer "Agent-Tool: claude-code" \
  --trailer "Agent-Model: claude-opus-5" \
  --trailer "Agent-Session-Id: $SESSION_ID"
```

`Co-authored-by` 回归它的本职——GitHub 归因、shortlog 里就是一个固定的 co-author。元数据各占一个 key，各自独立可查、可增可减。多 trailer 是完全惯用的写法，squash merge 时也会被保留合并。

这样前面那套查询就直接能用了：

```bash
git log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' \
    refs/agent/session/$ID/base..refs/agent/session/$ID/tip \
  | awk -v id="$ID" '$2 == id { print $1 }'
```

## 已有历史不用改写

新旧两种格式可以共存。写个函数同时认：

```bash
session_of() {
  local sha=$1 v
  v=$(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' "$sha")
  [ -n "$v" ] && { echo "$v"; return; }
  # 回退到旧的三段式
  git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Co-authored-by,valueonly)' "$sha" \
    | sed -n 's#.*/\([0-9a-f-]\{36\}\) <.*#\1#p'
}
```

跑一遍就能把旧 commit 的 session ref 重建出来，不需要 rebase。

## 另外

有些项目对 AI co-author trailer 有明确态度——Linux 内核、以及一部分要求 DCO sign-off 的项目，会把 `Co-authored-by` 当作真实的作者声明来处理，塞机器身份进去可能被要求改掉。这跟你要不要拆字段无关，但如果你会往外部仓库推，值得先确认对方的 contributing 规则。拆开之后正好也方便——需要时去掉 `Co-authored-by` 那一行，`Agent-*` 的元数据完全不受影响。

## 为什么不用分支

`checkout -b` 解决的是「隔离」，但它是最粗糙的那种隔离——它动了用户的工作区和 HEAD。
而「commit 时确保当前分支」是在拿环境状态当契约，这在 agent 场景下很脆：用户可能在另
一个终端切了分支，或者 agent 自己的某个工具调用里跑了 `checkout`。

正确的不变量不是「我在哪个分支上」，而是**「上一个 commit 是不是我预期的那个 SHA」**。

## ref 布局

```
refs/agent/session/{session_id}/base    session 起点，一次写定不再改
refs/agent/session/{session_id}/tip     每次 commit 后立刻推进
```

两个子 ref 是刻意的：files 后端下 `refs/agent/session/{id}` 和
`refs/agent/session/{id}/base` 不能共存（一个是文件、一个是目录）。要么统一用
`/base` `/tip`，要么统一只用一个，别混着来——否则第一个 session 好好的，第二个
换了命名方式就直接报错。

（只有 `heads/` `remotes/` `notes/` `HEAD` 是）。加上之后白得一份带时间戳、
按序的 session 进展记录，不用自己写日志文件。

## 各 hook 做什么

| hook | ref 方案（默认） | 分支方案 |
|------|-----------------|---------|
| SessionStart | 未提交的改动先问人（commit/stash/不管），然后记 `base = HEAD`。`USE_WORKTREE=1` 时开 detached worktree | 原来的建/切 `agent/{session_id}` 分支流程 |
| UserPromptSubmit | base 缺失就补记；`HEAD != tip` 时用 `systemMessage` 提醒（中间有别的 commit，或做过 rewind/reset），不阻塞 | 当前不在 agent 分支就 checkout，失败则 block |
| Stop | 在**当前分支**上 commit，然后 CAS 推进 tip | 先切到 agent 分支再 commit，同样推进 tip |

base 在三处都可能被记下（SessionStart → UserPromptSubmit → Stop 的第一个 commit），
谁先到算谁的，已存在就不动。所以**只装 Stop hook 也能工作**，SessionStart 不是必需的。

commit 后立刻更新 tip、而不是等 session 结束，有两个好处：一是崩溃安全，agent 中途挂

`base.agent_branch_mode(cwd, session_id)`：

1. `AGENT_BRANCH=1` → 分支方案；`AGENT_BRANCH=0` → 强制 ref 方案
2. 当前已经在 agent 分支上（`agent/{id}` 或旧的 `agent_{id}`）→ 分支方案
3. 这个 session 已经有对应的 agent 分支（人只是临时切走了）→ 分支方案

USE_WORKTREE=1 ~/work/sources/venv/bin/python ~/work/sources/sessionstart_hook.py
```

```json

"Stop":             [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../stop_hook.py -q",          "timeout": 300}]}],

```

refs/agent/session/{session_id}/tip     每次 commit 后立刻推进
```

两个子 ref 是刻意的：files 后端下 `refs/agent/session/{id}` 和
`refs/agent/session/{id}/base` 不能共存（一个是文件、一个是目录）。要么统一用
`/base` `/tip`，要么统一只用一个，别混着来——否则第一个 session 好好的，第二个
换了命名方式就直接报错。

`--create-reflog` 必须显式加：`refs/agent/` 不在默认开 reflog 的命名空间里
（只有 `heads/` `remotes/` `notes/` `HEAD` 是）。加上之后白得一份带时间戳、

> 2026.8.31 之前的做法：每个 session 一个 `agent_{session_id}` 分支，

## 为什么不用分支

`checkout -b` 解决的是「隔离」，但它是最粗糙的那种隔离——它动了用户的工作区和 HEAD。
而「commit 时确保当前分支」是在拿环境状态当契约，这在 agent 场景下很脆：用户可能在另
一个终端切了分支，或者 agent 自己的某个工具调用里跑了 `checkout`。

正确的不变量不是「我在哪个分支上」，而是**「上一个 commit 是不是我预期的那个 SHA」**。

## ref 布局

```
refs/agent/session/{session_id}/base    session 起点，一次写定不再改
refs/agent/session/{session_id}/tip     每次 commit 后立刻推进
```

两个子 ref 是刻意的：files 后端下 `refs/agent/session/{id}` 和
`refs/agent/session/{id}/base` 不能共存（一个是文件、一个是目录）。要么统一用
`/base` `/tip`，要么统一只用一个，别混着来——否则第一个 session 好好的，第二个
换了命名方式就直接报错。

`--create-reflog` 必须显式加：`refs/agent/` 不在默认开 reflog 的命名空间里
（只有 `heads/` `remotes/` `notes/` `HEAD` 是）。加上之后白得一份带时间戳、
按序的 session 进展记录，不用自己写日志文件。

## 各 hook 做什么

| hook | ref 方案（默认） | 分支方案 |
|------|-----------------|---------|
| SessionStart | 未提交的改动先问人（commit/stash/不管），然后记 `base = HEAD`。`USE_WORKTREE=1` 时开 detached worktree | 原来的建/切 `agent/{session_id}` 分支流程 |
| UserPromptSubmit | base 缺失就补记；`HEAD != tip` 时用 `systemMessage` 提醒（中间有别的 commit，或做过 rewind/reset），不阻塞 | 当前不在 agent 分支就 checkout，失败则 block |
| Stop | 在**当前分支**上 commit，然后 CAS 推进 tip | 先切到 agent 分支再 commit，同样推进 tip |

base 在三处都可能被记下（SessionStart → UserPromptSubmit → Stop 的第一个 commit），
谁先到算谁的，已存在就不动。所以**只装 Stop hook 也能工作**，SessionStart 不是必需的。

commit 后立刻更新 tip、而不是等 session 结束，有两个好处：一是崩溃安全，agent 中途挂
了、或者用户 `reset --hard` 了，对象从第一个 commit 起就被 ref 锚定，`gc` 碰不到；
二是 tip 的 reflog 自动变成 session 日志。

`base.agent_branch_mode(cwd, session_id)`：

1. `AGENT_BRANCH=1` → 分支方案；`AGENT_BRANCH=0` → 强制 ref 方案
2. 当前已经在 agent 分支上（`agent/{id}` 或旧的 `agent_{id}`）→ 分支方案
3. 这个 session 已经有对应的 agent 分支（人只是临时切走了）→ 分支方案
4. 以上都不满足 → ref 方案

```bash
# 分支方案（老仓库、或想让每个 session 独占一个分支）
AGENT_BRANCH=1 ~/work/sources/venv/bin/python ~/work/sources/stop_hook.py -q

USE_WORKTREE=1 ~/work/sources/venv/bin/python ~/work/sources/sessionstart_hook.py
```

`~/.claude/settings.json` 里已装的三个 hook：

```json
"SessionStart":     [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../sessionstart_hook.py",     "timeout": 300}]}],
"Stop":             [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../stop_hook.py -q",          "timeout": 300}]}],
"UserPromptSubmit": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../userpromptsubmit_hook.py", "timeout": 300}]}]
```

stdout 写：提示走 stderr，异常写进 `_traj/error.txt`，任何情况都 `exit 0`。

```bash

```

agent 有独立的工作区和独立的 HEAD，用户那边完全无感。`--detach` 是刻意的——不建分支

Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

| SessionStart | 未提交的改动先问人（commit/stash/不管），然后记 `base = HEAD`。`USE_WORKTREE=1` 时开 detached worktree | 原来的建/切 `agent/{session_id}` 分支流程 |
| UserPromptSubmit | base 缺失就补记；`HEAD != tip` 时用 `systemMessage` 提醒（中间有别的 commit，或做过 rewind/reset），不阻塞 | 当前不在 agent 分支就 checkout，失败则 block |
| Stop | 在**当前分支**上 commit，然后 CAS 推进 tip | 先切到 agent 分支再 commit，同样推进 tip |

base 在三处都可能被记下（SessionStart → UserPromptSubmit → Stop 的第一个 commit），
谁先到算谁的，已存在就不动。所以**只装 Stop hook 也能工作**，SessionStart 不是必需的。

commit 后立刻更新 tip、而不是等 session 结束，有两个好处：一是崩溃安全，agent 中途挂
了、或者用户 `reset --hard` 了，对象从第一个 commit 起就被 ref 锚定，`gc` 碰不到；
二是 tip 的 reflog 自动变成 session 日志。

## 两种方案怎么选

`base.agent_branch_mode(cwd, session_id)`：

1. `AGENT_BRANCH=1` → 分支方案；`AGENT_BRANCH=0` → 强制 ref 方案
2. 当前已经在 agent 分支上（`agent/{id}` 或旧的 `agent_{id}`）→ 分支方案
3. 这个 session 已经有对应的 agent 分支（人只是临时切走了）→ 分支方案
4. 以上都不满足 → ref 方案

装 hook 时按项目填，例如：

```bash
# 分支方案（老仓库、或想让每个 session 独占一个分支）
AGENT_BRANCH=1 ~/work/sources/venv/bin/python ~/work/sources/stop_hook.py -q

# ref 方案 + worktree 隔离（多个 claude 进程同时在跑）
USE_WORKTREE=1 ~/work/sources/venv/bin/python ~/work/sources/sessionstart_hook.py
```

`~/.claude/settings.json` 里已装的三个 hook：

```json
"SessionStart":     [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../sessionstart_hook.py",     "timeout": 300}]}],
"Stop":             [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../stop_hook.py -q",          "timeout": 300}]}],
"UserPromptSubmit": [{"hooks": [{"type": "command", "command": ".../userpromptsubmit_hook.py", "timeout": 300}]}]
```

SessionStart 的 stdout 会被当作 context 注入会话，所以 `sessionstart_hook.py` 一律不往
stdout 写：提示走 stderr，异常写进 `_traj/error.txt`，任何情况都 `exit 0`。
不想让它在工作区脏的时候弹交互窗口，就加 `-q`——那时它只记 base ref，别的都不做。

Windows：`set AGENT_BRANCH=1 && C:\work\sources\venv\Scripts\python.exe C:\work\sources\stop_hook.py -q`

## 需要隔离时用 worktree，不是分支

```bash
git worktree add --detach ../proj_agent_{session_id} $BASE
```

agent 有独立的工作区和独立的 HEAD，用户那边完全无感。`--detach` 是刻意的——不建分支
名，省掉命名冲突和清理。结束后 `git worktree remove`，commit 对象留在共享的 object
store 里，靠 tip ref 锚定。

## commit trailer

```
Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Agent-Tool: claude-code
Agent-Model: claude-opus-5
Agent-Session-Id: b47c8939-8ae6-4c1b-b9b2-f89c387b3e77
```

旧的三段式把工具/模型/session 三样东西按位置编码塞进了 `Co-authored-by` 的 name 位。
git 不报错（name 就是 `<` 之前的自由文本），但有实际代价：

1. `git shortlog -s --group=trailer:Co-authored-by` 会被打爆——每个 session 都是一个
   不同的「人」，跑几百个 session 之后没法看，mailmap 也救不了
2. GitHub 按 email 匹配账号，所有 session 折叠成一个 co-author，但显示名是那串 UUID
3. 位置编码不可扩展：想加 `Agent-Version`，或者分隔符 `/` 出现在模型名里就歧义了
4. 查询要额外剥一层

拆开之后 `Co-authored-by` 回归本职（GitHub 归因、shortlog 里就是一个固定的
co-author），元数据各占一个 key，各自独立可查、可增可减。多 trailer 是完全惯用的写法，
squash merge 时也会被保留合并。

trailer **每次 commit 都显式传** `--trailer`（git 2.32+），不依赖 hook 或
`commit.template`——显式参数不依赖任何环境状态，也就不需要「确保当前分支」这种检查。

> 有些项目对 AI co-author trailer 有明确态度——Linux 内核、以及一部分要求 DCO
> sign-off 的项目会把 `Co-authored-by` 当作真实的作者声明。往外部仓库推之前先确认
> 对方的 contributing 规则；拆开之后正好方便：去掉 `Co-authored-by` 那一行，
> `Agent-*` 的元数据完全不受影响。

## 查询与清理

`agent-sessions.py`（`-C <repo>` 指定仓库，默认当前目录）：

```bash
agent-sessions.py list              # 列出所有 session：commit 数、最后一次提交
agent-sessions.py log <id>          # 这个 session 干了什么（base..tip）
agent-sessions.py log <id> --only   # 只列 trailer 属于它的 commit（范围里可能混着别人的）
agent-sessions.py diff <id>         # 这个 session 的总 diff
agent-sessions.py reflog <id>       # 进展日志（带时间戳）
agent-sessions.py of <rev>          # 某个 commit 属于哪个 session
agent-sessions.py rebuild           # 从 commit trailer 重建 ref（新旧格式都认）
agent-sessions.py prune <id>...     # 删 ref；--all / --older-than 30 / -y
```

session id 可以只写前几位，不唯一时会列出候选。

改完 hook 跑一遍自测（在临时仓库里做，不碰任何真实项目）：

```bash
test/agent-session-refs.sh          # 21 项
KEEP=1 test/agent-session-refs.sh   # 保留现场供检查
```

对应的原生 git 命令：

```bash
# 这个 session 干了什么
git log refs/agent/session/$ID/base..refs/agent/session/$ID/tip

# 列所有 session
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:lstrip=3) %(objectname:short)' \
    'refs/agent/session/*/tip'

# 从 trailer 反查（ref 丢了或过时了的时候）
git log --all --format='%H %(trailers:key=Agent-Session-Id,valueonly)' \
  | grep " $ID$"

# 过期清理：ref 是派生数据，删了不丢信息
git for-each-ref --format='%(refname)' 'refs/agent/session/*' \
  | xargs -n1 git update-ref -d
```

## 已有历史不用改写

新旧两种格式共存，`base.git_session_of_commit()` 同时认：先取
`Agent-Session-Id`，取不到再从旧的三段式 `Co-authored-by` 里剥出 UUID。
`agent-sessions.py rebuild` 跑一遍就能把旧 commit 的 session ref 重建出来
（base = 该 session 第一个 commit 的父提交，tip = 最后一个 commit），不需要 rebase。

原来的 `agent_{session_id}` / `agent/{session_id}` 分支不用删，也不用 merge——
它们只是历史上的 ref，commit 本身照样能被 trailer 和新的 session ref 找到。

## 并发写

多个 ref 一起改用 `git update-ref --stdin`（`start` / `update` / `prepare` / `commit`），
`update <ref> <new> <old>` 带旧值就是 compare-and-swap，并发下不会覆盖别人的写入。
CAS 撞车时（另一个 hook 进程、或人手动动过），如果仓库里的 tip 是新 commit 的祖先，
说明我们的 commit 就长在它上面，直接推进；否则如实报错，不强推。

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> Any:

def shortcut_launch() -> Any:

def parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:
    """Parse command-line arguments"""
    if argv is None:
        argv = sys.argv[1:]
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.set_defaults(func=cmd_dag)

    app.add_common_arguments(parser)
    parser.add_argument(
        '-c',
        '--count',
        '--max-count',
        metavar='<count>',
        type=int,
        default=100000,
        help='number of commits to display',
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        'args', nargs=argparse.REMAINDER, metavar='<args>', help='git log arguments'
    )
    args, rest = parser.parse_known_args(args=argv)
    if rest:
        # splice unknown arguments to the beginning ~

        args.args[:0] = rest
    return args

from __future__ import annotations
import datetime
import json
from collections.abc import Iterator

from .. import core
from .. import utils
from ..i18n import N_
from ..models import prefs

# put summary at the end b/c it can contain
# any number of funky characters, including the separator
LOGFMT = r'format:%H%x01%P%x01%d%x01%an%x01%ad%x01%ae%x01%s'
LOGSEP = chr(0x01)
STAGE = 'STAGE'
WORKTREE = 'WORKTREE'


class CommitFactory:
    root_generation = 0
    commits = {}

    @classmethod
    def reset(cls) -> None:
        cls.commits.clear()
        cls.root_generation = 0

    @classmethod
    def new(
        cls, context, oid: str | None = None, log_entry: str | None = None
    ) -> Commit:
        if not oid and log_entry:
            oid = log_entry[: context.model.oid_len]
        try:
            commit = cls.commits[oid]
            if log_entry and not commit.parsed:
                commit.parse(log_entry)
            cls.root_generation = max(commit.generation, cls.root_generation)
        except KeyError:
            commit = Commit(context, oid=oid, log_entry=log_entry)
            if not log_entry:
                cls.root_generation += 1
                commit.generation = max(commit.generation, cls.root_generation)
            cls.commits[oid] = commit
        return commit


class DAG:
    def __init__(self, ref: str, count: int) -> None:
        self.ref = ref
        self.count = count
        self.display_status = True
        # When true, an orphan-rooted chain keeps its column reserved
        # for the rest of the layout pass so an unrelated chain cannot
        # land on the same column.
        self.orphan_isolate = False
        self.overrides = {}

    def set_ref(self, ref: str) -> bool:
        changed = ref != self.ref
        if changed:
            self.ref = ref
        return changed

    def set_count(self, count: int) -> bool:
        changed = count != self.count
        if changed:
            self.count = count
        return changed

    def set_arguments(self, args) -> None:
        if args is None:
            return
        if self.set_count(args.count):
            self.overrides['count'] = args.count

        isolate = getattr(args, 'orphan_isolate', None)
        if isolate is not None and self.set_orphan_isolate(isolate):
            self.overrides['orphan_isolate'] = bool(isolate)

        if hasattr(args, 'args') and args.args:
            ref = core.list2cmdline(args.args)
            if self.set_ref(ref):
                self.overrides['ref'] = ref

    def set_orphan_isolate(self, value) -> bool:
        if isinstance(value, str):
            normalized = value.strip().lower() in ('1', 'true', 'yes', 'on')
        else:
            normalized = bool(value)
        if normalized == self.orphan_isolate:
            return False
        self.orphan_isolate = normalized
        return True

    def set_display_status(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """Should we display the worktree status?"""
        self.display_status = enabled

    def overridden(self, opt: str) -> bool:
        return opt in self.overrides

    def paths(self) -> list[str]:
        all_refs = utils.shell_split(self.ref)
        if '--' in all_refs:
            all_refs = all_refs[all_refs.index('--') :]

        return [p for p in all_refs if p and core.exists(p)]


class Commit:
    root_generation = 0

    __slots__ = (
        'context',
        'oid',
        'summary',
        'parents',
        'children',
        'branches',
        'tags',
        'author',
        'authdate',
        'email',
        'generation',
        'column',
        'row',
        'parsed',
    )

    def __init__(
        self, context, oid: str | None = None, log_entry: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self.context = context
        self.oid = oid
        self.summary: str | None = None
        self.parents: list[Commit] = []
        self.children = []
        self.tags: list[str] = []
        self.branches = []
        self.email: str | None = None
        self.author: str | None = None
        self.authdate: str | None = None
        self.parsed = False
        self.generation = CommitFactory.root_generation
        self.column = None
        self.row = None
        if log_entry:
            self.parse(log_entry)

    def parse(self, log_entry: str, sep: str = LOGSEP):
        oid_len = self.context.model.oid_len
        self.oid = log_entry[:oid_len]
        after_oid = log_entry[oid_len + 1 :]
        details = after_oid.split(sep, 5)
        (parents, tags, author, authdate, email, summary) = details

        self.summary = summary if summary else ''
        self.author = author if author else ''
        self.authdate = authdate if authdate else ''
        self.email = email if email else ''

        if parents:
            generation = None
            for parent_oid in parents.split(' '):
                parent = CommitFactory.new(self.context, oid=parent_oid)
                parent.children.append(self)
                if generation is None:
                    generation = parent.generation + 1
                self.parents.append(parent)
                generation = max(parent.generation + 1, generation)
            self.generation = generation

        if tags:
            for tag in tags[2:-1].split(', '):
                self.add_label(tag)

        self.parsed = True
        return self

    def add_label(self, tag: str) -> None:
        """Add tag/branch labels from `git log --decorate ....`"""
        if tag.startswith('tag: '):
            tag = tag[5:]  # strip off "tag: " leaving refs/tags/
        if tag.startswith('refs/heads/'):
            branch = tag[11:]
            self.branches.append(branch)
        if tag.startswith('refs/'):
            # strip off refs/ leaving just tags/XXX remotes/XXX heads/XXX
            tag = tag[5:]
        if tag.endswith('/HEAD'):
            return

        # Git 2.4 Release Notes (draft)
        # =============================
        #
        # Backward compatibility warning(s)
        # ---------------------------------
        #
        # This release has a few changes in the user-visible output from
        # Porcelain commands. These are not meant to be parsed by scripts, but
        # the users still may want to be aware of the changes:
        #
        # * Output from "git log --decorate" (and "%d" format specifier used in
        #   the userformat "--format=<string>" parameter "git log" family of
        #   command takes) used to list "HEAD" just like other tips of branch
        #   names, separated with a comma in between.  E.g.
        #
        #      $ git log --decorate -1 main
        #      commit bdb0f6788fa5e3cacc4315e9ff318a27b2676ff4 (HEAD, main)
        #      ...
        #
        # This release updates the output slightly when HEAD refers to the tip
        # of a branch whose name is also shown in the output.  The above is
        # shown as:
        #
        #      $ git log --decorate -1 main
        #      commit bdb0f6788fa5e3cacc4315e9ff318a27b2676ff4 (HEAD -> main)
        #      ...
        #
        # C.f. http://thread.gmane.org/gmane.linux.kernel/1931234
        head_arrow = 'HEAD -> '
        if tag.startswith(head_arrow):
            self.tags.append('HEAD')
            self.add_label(tag[len(head_arrow) :])
        else:
            self.tags.append(tag)

    def __str__(self) -> str | None:
        return self.oid

    def data(self) -> dict[str, str | None | list[str | None] | list[str]]:
        return {
            'oid': self.oid,
            'summary': self.summary,
            'author': self.author,
            'authdate': self.authdate,
            'parents': [p.oid for p in self.parents],
            'tags': self.tags,
        }

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.data(), sort_keys=True, indent=4, default=list)

    def is_fork(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the node is a fork"""
        return len(self.children) > 1

    def is_merge(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the node is a fork"""
        return len(self.parents) > 1


class RepoReader:
    def __init__(self, context, params: DAG, allow_git_init: bool = True) -> None:
        self.context = context
        self.params = params
        self.git = context.git
        self.returncode = 0
        self._allow_git_init = allow_git_init
        self._objects: dict[str, Commit] = {}
        self._cmd = [
            'git',
            '-c',
            'log.abbrevCommit=false',
            '-c',
            'log.showSignature=false',
            'log',
            '--topo-order',
            '--decorate=full',
            '--pretty=' + LOGFMT,
        ]
        self._cached = False
        """Indicates that all data has been read"""
        self._topo_list = []
        """List of commits objects in topological order"""

    cached = property(lambda self: self._cached)
    """Return True when no commits remain to be read"""

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._topo_list)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        CommitFactory.reset()
        self._cached = False
        self._topo_list = []

    def get(self) -> Iterator[Commit]:
        """Generator function returns Commit objects found by the params"""
        if self._cached:
            for commit in self._topo_list:
                yield commit
            return

        self.reset()
        ref_args = utils.shell_split(self.params.ref)
        cmd = (
            self._cmd
            + ['-%d' % self.params.count]
            + ['--date=%s' % prefs.logdate(self.context)]
            + ['--no-patch']
            + ref_args
        )
        commit = None

        # When _allow_git_init is True then we detect the "git init" state
        # by checking whether any local branches currently exist.
        if not self._allow_git_init or self.context.model.local_branches:
            status, out, _ = core.run_command(cmd)
            oid_len = self.context.model.oid_len
            for log_entry in reversed(out.splitlines()):
                if not log_entry:
                    break
                oid = log_entry[:oid_len]
                try:
                    commit = self._objects[oid]
                except KeyError:
                    try:
                        commit = CommitFactory.new(self.context, log_entry=log_entry)
                    except (KeyError, ValueError):
                        continue
                    self._objects[commit.oid] = commit
                    self._topo_list.append(commit)
                yield commit
        else:
            # git init
            status = 0
        self._top_commit = commit
        self._cached = True
        self.returncode = status

    def get_worktree_commits(self) -> tuple[Commit | None, Commit | None]:
        """A Commit object that represents unstaged modified changes in a worktree"""
        if self.returncode != 0 or not self.params.display_status:
            return None, None
        context = self.context
        model = context.model
        if not model.modified and not model.staged and not model.unmerged:
            return None, None
        parents = []
        parent_commit = self._top_commit
        status, head, _ = context.git.rev_parse('HEAD', _readonly=True)
        if status != 0:
            # "git init" should include worktree and stage entries.
            # We do not early out with None and leave the parents list empty.
            pass
        elif parent_commit:
            # Is the top-most commit also our current HEAD?
            # If so we'll include worktree and stage placeholder commits
            # otherwise we should early out and omit these entries.
            if head != parent_commit.oid:
                return None, None
            parents = [parent_commit]

        author, email = context.cfg.get_author()
        if model.commitmsg:
            summary = model.commitmsg.split('\n', 1)[0]
        else:
            summary = ''

        if summary:
            stage_summary = f'STAGE: {summary}'
            worktree_summary = f'WORKTREE: {summary}'
        else:
            stage_summary = N_('STAGE: changes ready to commit')

    root_generation = 0

    __slots__ = (
        'context',
        'oid',
        'summary',
        'parents',
        'children',
        'branches',
        'tags',
        'author',
        'authdate',
        'email',
        'generation',
        'column',
        'row',
        'parsed',
    )

    def __init__(
        self, context, oid: str | None = None, log_entry: str | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self.context = context
        self.oid = oid
        self.summary: str | None = None
        self.parents: list[Commit] = []
        self.children = []
        self.tags: list[str] = []
        self.branches = []
        self.email: str | None = None
        self.author: str | None = None
        self.authdate: str | None = None
        self.parsed = False
        self.generation = CommitFactory.root_generation
        self.column = None
        self.row = None
        if log_entry:
            self.parse(log_entry)

    def parse(self, log_entry: str, sep: str = LOGSEP):
        oid_len = self.context.model.oid_len
        self.oid = log_entry[:oid_len]
        after_oid = log_entry[oid_len + 1 :]
        details = after_oid.split(sep, 5)
        (parents, tags, author, authdate, email, summary) = details

        self.summary = summary if summary else ''
        self.author = author if author else ''
        self.authdate = authdate if authdate else ''
        self.email = email if email else ''

        if parents:
            generation = None
            for parent_oid in parents.split(' '):
                parent = CommitFactory.new(self.context, oid=parent_oid)
                parent.children.append(self)
                if generation is None:
                    generation = parent.generation + 1
                self.parents.append(parent)
                generation = max(parent.generation + 1, generation)
            self.generation = generation

        if tags:
            for tag in tags[2:-1].split(', '):
                self.add_label(tag)

        self.parsed = True
        return self

    def add_label(self, tag: str) -> None:
        """Add tag/branch labels from `git log --decorate ....`"""
        if tag.startswith('tag: '):
            tag = tag[5:]  # strip off "tag: " leaving refs/tags/
        if tag.startswith('refs/heads/'):
            branch = tag[11:]
            self.branches.append(branch)
        if tag.startswith('refs/'):
            # strip off refs/ leaving just tags/XXX remotes/XXX heads/XXX
            tag = tag[5:]
        if tag.endswith('/HEAD'):
            return

        # Git 2.4 Release Notes (draft)
        # =============================
        #
        # Backward compatibility warning(s)
        # ---------------------------------
        #
        # This release has a few changes in the user-visible output from
        # Porcelain commands. These are not meant to be parsed by scripts, but
        # the users still may want to be aware of the changes:
        #
        # * Output from "git log --decorate" (and "%d" format specifier used in
        #   the userformat "--format=<string>" parameter "git log" family of
        #   command takes) used to list "HEAD" just like other tips of branch
        #   names, separated with a comma in between.  E.g.
        #
        #      $ git log --decorate -1 main
        #      commit bdb0f6788fa5e3cacc4315e9ff318a27b2676ff4 (HEAD, main)
        #      ...
        #
        # This release updates the output slightly when HEAD refers to the tip
        # of a branch whose name is also shown in the output.  The above is
        # shown as:
        #
        #      $ git log --decorate -1 main
        #      commit bdb0f6788fa5e3cacc4315e9ff318a27b2676ff4 (HEAD -> main)
        #      ...
        #
        # C.f. http://thread.gmane.org/gmane.linux.kernel/1931234
        head_arrow = 'HEAD -> '
        if tag.startswith(head_arrow):
            self.tags.append('HEAD')
            self.add_label(tag[len(head_arrow) :])
        else:
            self.tags.append(tag)

    def __str__(self) -> str | None:
        return self.oid

    def data(self) -> dict[str, str | None | list[str | None] | list[str]]:
        return {
            'oid': self.oid,
            'summary': self.summary,
            'author': self.author,
            'authdate': self.authdate,
            'parents': [p.oid for p in self.parents],
            'tags': self.tags,
        }

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.data(), sort_keys=True, indent=4, default=list)

    def is_fork(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the node is a fork"""
        return len(self.children) > 1

    def is_merge(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the node is a fork"""
        return len(self.parents) > 1


class RepoReader:
    def __init__(self, context, params: DAG, allow_git_init: bool = True) -> None:
        self.context = context
        self.params = params
        self.git = context.git
        self.returncode = 0
        self._allow_git_init = allow_git_init
        self._objects: dict[str, Commit] = {}
        self._cmd = [
            'git',
            '-c',
            'log.abbrevCommit=false',
            '-c',
            'log.showSignature=false',
            'log',
            '--topo-order',
            '--decorate=full',
            '--pretty=' + LOGFMT,
        ]
        self._cached = False
        """Indicates that all data has been read"""
        self._topo_list = []
        """List of commits objects in topological order"""

    cached = property(lambda self: self._cached)
    """Return True when no commits remain to be read"""

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._topo_list)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        CommitFactory.reset()
        self._cached = False
        self._topo_list = []

    def get(self) -> Iterator[Commit]:
        """Generator function returns Commit objects found by the params"""
        if self._cached:
            for commit in self._topo_list:
                yield commit
            return

        self.reset()
        ref_args = utils.shell_split(self.params.ref)
        cmd = (
            self._cmd
            + ['-%d' % self.params.count]
            + ['--date=%s' % prefs.logdate(self.context)]
            + ['--no-patch']
            + ref_args
        )
        commit = None

        # When _allow_git_init is True then we detect the "git init" state
        # by checking whether any local branches currently exist.
        if not self._allow_git_init or self.context.model.local_branches:
            status, out, _ = core.run_command(cmd)
            oid_len = self.context.model.oid_len
            for log_entry in reversed(out.splitlines()):
                if not log_entry:
                    break
                oid = log_entry[:oid_len]
                try:
                    commit = self._objects[oid]
                except KeyError:
                    try:
                        commit = CommitFactory.new(self.context, log_entry=log_entry)
                    except (KeyError, ValueError):
                        continue
                    self._objects[commit.oid] = commit
                    self._topo_list.append(commit)
                yield commit
        else:
            # git init
            status = 0
        self._top_commit = commit
        self._cached = True
        self.returncode = status

    def get_worktree_commits(self) -> tuple[Commit | None, Commit | None]:
        """A Commit object that represents unstaged modified changes in a worktree"""
        if self.returncode != 0 or not self.params.display_status:
            return None, None
        context = self.context
        model = context.model
        if not model.modified and not model.staged and not model.unmerged:
            return None, None
        parents = []
        parent_commit = self._top_commit
        status, head, _ = context.git.rev_parse('HEAD', _readonly=True)
        if status != 0:
            # "git init" should include worktree and stage entries.
            # We do not early out with None and leave the parents list empty.
            pass
        elif parent_commit:
            # Is the top-most commit also our current HEAD?
            # If so we'll include worktree and stage placeholder commits
            # otherwise we should early out and omit these entries.
            if head != parent_commit.oid:
                return None, None
            parents = [parent_commit]

        author, email = context.cfg.get_author()
        if model.commitmsg:
            summary = model.commitmsg.split('\n', 1)[0]
        else:
            summary = ''

        if summary:
            stage_summary = f'STAGE: {summary}'
            worktree_summary = f'WORKTREE: {summary}'
        else:
            stage_summary = N_('STAGE: changes ready to commit')
            worktree_summary = N_('WORKTREE: unstaged changes')
        authdate = get_date_for_current_time(context)

        stage_commit = None
        worktree_commit = None

        if model.staged:
            stage_commit = Commit(context, oid=STAGE)
            stage_commit.add_label(STAGE)
            stage_commit.parents = parents
            stage_commit.summary = stage_summary
            stage_commit.author = author
            stage_commit.email = email
            stage_commit.authdate = authdate
            stage_commit.parsed = True
            if parent_commit:
                parent_commit.children.append(stage_commit)
                stage_commit.generation = parent_commit.generation + 1
            # Update state for the subsequent WORKTREE pseudo-commit.
            parents = [stage_commit]
            parent_commit = stage_commit

        if model.modified or model.unmerged:
            worktree_commit = Commit(context, oid=WORKTREE)
            worktree_commit.add_label(WORKTREE)
            worktree_commit.parents = parents
            worktree_commit.summary = worktree_summary
            worktree_commit.author = author
            worktree_commit.email = email
            worktree_commit.authdate = authdate
            worktree_commit.parsed = True
            if parent_commit:
                parent_commit.children.append(worktree_commit)
                worktree_commit.generation = parent_commit.generation + 1

        return stage_commit, worktree_commit

    elif logdate == DateFormat.ISO_STRICT:

    elif logdate == DateFormat.RAW:

    elif logdate == DateFormat.RELATIVE:

    elif logdate == DateFormat.RFC:
        authdate = now.strftime('%a, %e %b %Y %H:%M:%S %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.SHORT:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.UNIX:
        authdate = now.strftime('%s')
    elif DateFormat.is_custom(logdate):
        fmt = DateFormat.get_custom_format(logdate)

class CommitFactory:
    root_generation = 0
    commits = {}

    @classmethod
    def reset(cls) -> None:
        cls.commits.clear()
        cls.root_generation = 0

    @classmethod
    def new(
        cls, context, oid: str | None = None, log_entry: str | None = None
    ) -> Commit:
        if not oid and log_entry:
            oid = log_entry[: context.model.oid_len]
        try:
            commit = cls.commits[oid]
            if log_entry and not commit.parsed:
                commit.parse(log_entry)
            cls.root_generation = max(commit.generation, cls.root_generation)
        except KeyError:
            commit = Commit(context, oid=oid, log_entry=log_entry)
            if not log_entry:
                cls.root_generation += 1
                commit.generation = max(commit.generation, cls.root_generation)
            cls.commits[oid] = commit
        return commit


class DAG:
    def __init__(self, ref: str, count: int) -> None:
        self.ref = ref
        self.count = count
        self.display_status = True
        # When true, an orphan-rooted chain keeps its column reserved
        # for the rest of the layout pass so an unrelated chain cannot
        # land on the same column.
        self.orphan_isolate = False
        self.overrides = {}

    def set_ref(self, ref: str) -> bool:
        changed = ref != self.ref
        if changed:
            self.ref = ref
        return changed

    def set_count(self, count: int) -> bool:
        changed = count != self.count
        if changed:
            self.count = count
        return changed

    def set_arguments(self, args) -> None:
        if args is None:
            return
        if self.set_count(args.count):
            self.overrides['count'] = args.count

        isolate = getattr(args, 'orphan_isolate', None)
        if isolate is not None and self.set_orphan_isolate(isolate):
            self.overrides['orphan_isolate'] = bool(isolate)

        if hasattr(args, 'args') and args.args:
            ref = core.list2cmdline(args.args)
            if self.set_ref(ref):
                self.overrides['ref'] = ref

    def set_orphan_isolate(self, value) -> bool:
        if isinstance(value, str):
            normalized = value.strip().lower() in ('1', 'true', 'yes', 'on')
        else:
            normalized = bool(value)
        if normalized == self.orphan_isolate:
            return False
        self.orphan_isolate = normalized
        return True

    def set_display_status(self, enabled: bool) -> None:
        """Should we display the worktree status?"""
        self.display_status = enabled

    def overridden(self, opt: str) -> bool:
        return opt in self.overrides

    def paths(self) -> list[str]:
        all_refs = utils.shell_split(self.ref)
        if '--' in all_refs:
            all_refs = all_refs[all_refs.index('--') :]

        return [p for p in all_refs if p and core.exists(p)]

    def __init__(self, context, params: DAG, allow_git_init: bool = True) -> None:
        self.context = context
        self.params = params
        self.git = context.git

        self._allow_git_init = allow_git_init

        self._cmd = [
            'git',

            'log.abbrevCommit=false',
            '-c',
            'log.showSignature=false',
            'log',
            '--topo-order',
            '--decorate=full',

        self._topo_list = []

    cached = property(lambda self: self._cached)
    """Return True when no commits remain to be read"""

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._topo_list)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        CommitFactory.reset()
        self._cached = False
        self._topo_list = []

    def get(self) -> Iterator[Commit]:
        """Generator function returns Commit objects found by the params"""
        if self._cached:
            for commit in self._topo_list:
                yield commit
            return

        self.reset()
        ref_args = utils.shell_split(self.params.ref)
        cmd = (
            self._cmd
            + ['-%d' % self.params.count]
            + ['--date=%s' % prefs.logdate(self.context)]
            + ['--no-patch']
            + ref_args
        )
        commit = None

        # When _allow_git_init is True then we detect the "git init" state
        # by checking whether any local branches currently exist.
        if not self._allow_git_init or self.context.model.local_branches:
            status, out, _ = core.run_command(cmd)
            oid_len = self.context.model.oid_len
            for log_entry in reversed(out.splitlines()):
                if not log_entry:
                    break
                oid = log_entry[:oid_len]
                try:
                    commit = self._objects[oid]
                except KeyError:
                    try:
                        commit = CommitFactory.new(self.context, log_entry=log_entry)
                    except (KeyError, ValueError):
                        continue
                    self._objects[commit.oid] = commit
                    self._topo_list.append(commit)
                yield commit
        else:
            # git init
            status = 0
        self._top_commit = commit
        self._cached = True
        self.returncode = status

    def get_worktree_commits(self) -> tuple[Commit | None, Commit | None]:
        """A Commit object that represents unstaged modified changes in a worktree"""
        if self.returncode != 0 or not self.params.display_status:
            return None, None
        context = self.context
        model = context.model
        if not model.modified and not model.staged and not model.unmerged:
            return None, None
        parents = []
        parent_commit = self._top_commit
        status, head, _ = context.git.rev_parse('HEAD', _readonly=True)
        if status != 0:
            # "git init" should include worktree and stage entries.
            # We do not early out with None and leave the parents list empty.
            pass
        elif parent_commit:
            # Is the top-most commit also our current HEAD?
            # If so we'll include worktree and stage placeholder commits
            # otherwise we should early out and omit these entries.
            if head != parent_commit.oid:
                return None, None
            parents = [parent_commit]

        author, email = context.cfg.get_author()
        if model.commitmsg:
            summary = model.commitmsg.split('\n', 1)[0]
        else:
            summary = ''

        if summary:
            stage_summary = f'STAGE: {summary}'
            worktree_summary = f'WORKTREE: {summary}'
        else:
            stage_summary = N_('STAGE: changes ready to commit')
            worktree_summary = N_('WORKTREE: unstaged changes')
        authdate = get_date_for_current_time(context)

        stage_commit = None
        worktree_commit = None

        if model.staged:
            stage_commit = Commit(context, oid=STAGE)
            stage_commit.add_label(STAGE)
            stage_commit.parents = parents
            stage_commit.summary = stage_summary
            stage_commit.author = author
            stage_commit.email = email
            stage_commit.authdate = authdate
            stage_commit.parsed = True
            if parent_commit:
                parent_commit.children.append(stage_commit)
                stage_commit.generation = parent_commit.generation + 1
            # Update state for the subsequent WORKTREE pseudo-commit.
            parents = [stage_commit]
            parent_commit = stage_commit

        if model.modified or model.unmerged:
            worktree_commit = Commit(context, oid=WORKTREE)
            worktree_commit.add_label(WORKTREE)
            worktree_commit.parents = parents
            worktree_commit.summary = worktree_summary
            worktree_commit.author = author
            worktree_commit.email = email
            worktree_commit.authdate = authdate
            worktree_commit.parsed = True
            if parent_commit:
                parent_commit.children.append(worktree_commit)
                worktree_commit.generation = parent_commit.generation + 1

        return stage_commit, worktree_commit

    def __getitem__(self, oid: str) -> Commit:
        return self._objects[oid]

    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Commit]]:
        return list(self._objects.items())

    """Return the current time formatted according to the cola.logdate configuration"""
    DateFormat = prefs.DateFormat
    logdate = prefs.logdate(context)
    now = datetime.datetime.now().astimezone()
    if logdate == DateFormat.DEFAULT:

    elif logdate == DateFormat.HUMAN:

    elif logdate == DateFormat.LOCAL:

    elif logdate == DateFormat.ISO:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.ISO_STRICT:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.RAW:
        authdate = now.strftime('%s %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.RELATIVE:
        authdate = '0 seconds ago'
    elif logdate == DateFormat.RFC:
        authdate = now.strftime('%a, %e %b %Y %H:%M:%S %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.SHORT:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.UNIX:

        # of a branch whose name is also shown in the output.  The above is
        # shown as:
        #
        #      $ git log --decorate -1 main
        #      commit bdb0f6788fa5e3cacc4315e9ff318a27b2676ff4 (HEAD -> main)
        #      ...
        #
        # C.f. http://thread.gmane.org/gmane.linux.kernel/1931234
        head_arrow = 'HEAD -> '
        if tag.startswith(head_arrow):
            self.tags.append('HEAD')
            self.add_label(tag[len(head_arrow) :])
        else:
            self.tags.append(tag)

    def __str__(self) -> str | None:
        return self.oid

    def data(self) -> dict[str, str | None | list[str | None] | list[str]]:
        return {
            'oid': self.oid,
            'summary': self.summary,
            'author': self.author,
            'authdate': self.authdate,
            'parents': [p.oid for p in self.parents],
            'tags': self.tags,
        }

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return json.dumps(self.data(), sort_keys=True, indent=4, default=list)

    def is_fork(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the node is a fork"""
        return len(self.children) > 1

    def is_merge(self) -> bool:
        """Returns True if the node is a fork"""
        return len(self.parents) > 1


class RepoReader:
    def __init__(self, context, params: DAG, allow_git_init: bool = True) -> None:
        self.context = context
        self.params = params
        self.git = context.git
        self.returncode = 0
        self._allow_git_init = allow_git_init
        self._objects: dict[str, Commit] = {}
        self._cmd = [
            'git',
            '-c',
            'log.abbrevCommit=false',
            '-c',
            'log.showSignature=false',
            'log',
            '--topo-order',
            '--decorate=full',
            '--pretty=' + LOGFMT,
        ]
        self._cached = False
        """Indicates that all data has been read"""
        self._topo_list = []
        """List of commits objects in topological order"""

    cached = property(lambda self: self._cached)
    """Return True when no commits remain to be read"""

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._topo_list)

    def reset(self) -> None:
        CommitFactory.reset()
        self._cached = False
        self._topo_list = []

    def get(self) -> Iterator[Commit]:
        """Generator function returns Commit objects found by the params"""
        if self._cached:
            for commit in self._topo_list:
                yield commit
            return

        self.reset()
        ref_args = utils.shell_split(self.params.ref)
        cmd = (
            self._cmd
            + ['-%d' % self.params.count]
            + ['--date=%s' % prefs.logdate(self.context)]
            + ['--no-patch']
            + ref_args
        )
        commit = None

        # When _allow_git_init is True then we detect the "git init" state
        # by checking whether any local branches currently exist.
        if not self._allow_git_init or self.context.model.local_branches:
            status, out, _ = core.run_command(cmd)
            oid_len = self.context.model.oid_len
            for log_entry in reversed(out.splitlines()):
                if not log_entry:
                    break
                oid = log_entry[:oid_len]
                try:
                    commit = self._objects[oid]
                except KeyError:
                    try:
                        commit = CommitFactory.new(self.context, log_entry=log_entry)
                    except (KeyError, ValueError):
                        continue
                    self._objects[commit.oid] = commit
                    self._topo_list.append(commit)
                yield commit
        else:
            # git init
            status = 0
        self._top_commit = commit
        self._cached = True
        self.returncode = status

    def get_worktree_commits(self) -> tuple[Commit | None, Commit | None]:
        """A Commit object that represents unstaged modified changes in a worktree"""
        if self.returncode != 0 or not self.params.display_status:
            return None, None
        context = self.context
        model = context.model
        if not model.modified and not model.staged and not model.unmerged:
            return None, None
        parents = []
        parent_commit = self._top_commit
        status, head, _ = context.git.rev_parse('HEAD', _readonly=True)
        if status != 0:
            # "git init" should include worktree and stage entries.
            # We do not early out with None and leave the parents list empty.
            pass
        elif parent_commit:
            # Is the top-most commit also our current HEAD?
            # If so we'll include worktree and stage placeholder commits
            # otherwise we should early out and omit these entries.
            if head != parent_commit.oid:
                return None, None
            parents = [parent_commit]

        author, email = context.cfg.get_author()
        if model.commitmsg:
            summary = model.commitmsg.split('\n', 1)[0]
        else:
            summary = ''

        if summary:
            stage_summary = f'STAGE: {summary}'
            worktree_summary = f'WORKTREE: {summary}'
        else:
            stage_summary = N_('STAGE: changes ready to commit')
            worktree_summary = N_('WORKTREE: unstaged changes')
        authdate = get_date_for_current_time(context)

        stage_commit = None
        worktree_commit = None

        if model.staged:
            stage_commit = Commit(context, oid=STAGE)
            stage_commit.add_label(STAGE)
            stage_commit.parents = parents
            stage_commit.summary = stage_summary
            stage_commit.author = author
            stage_commit.email = email
            stage_commit.authdate = authdate
            stage_commit.parsed = True
            if parent_commit:
                parent_commit.children.append(stage_commit)
                stage_commit.generation = parent_commit.generation + 1
            # Update state for the subsequent WORKTREE pseudo-commit.
            parents = [stage_commit]
            parent_commit = stage_commit

        if model.modified or model.unmerged:
            worktree_commit = Commit(context, oid=WORKTREE)
            worktree_commit.add_label(WORKTREE)
            worktree_commit.parents = parents
            worktree_commit.summary = worktree_summary
            worktree_commit.author = author
            worktree_commit.email = email
            worktree_commit.authdate = authdate
            worktree_commit.parsed = True
            if parent_commit:
                parent_commit.children.append(worktree_commit)
                worktree_commit.generation = parent_commit.generation + 1

        return stage_commit, worktree_commit

    def __getitem__(self, oid: str) -> Commit:
        return self._objects[oid]

    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Commit]]:
        return list(self._objects.items())


def get_date_for_current_time(context) -> str:
    """Return the current time formatted according to the cola.logdate configuration"""
    DateFormat = prefs.DateFormat
    logdate = prefs.logdate(context)
    now = datetime.datetime.now().astimezone()
    if logdate == DateFormat.DEFAULT:
        authdate = now.strftime('%c %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.HUMAN:
        authdate = now.strftime('%a %b %d %H:%M')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.LOCAL:
        authdate = now.strftime('%c')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.ISO:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.ISO_STRICT:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.RAW:
        authdate = now.strftime('%s %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.RELATIVE:
        authdate = '0 seconds ago'
    elif logdate == DateFormat.RFC:
        authdate = now.strftime('%a, %e %b %Y %H:%M:%S %z')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.SHORT:
        authdate = now.strftime('%Y-%m-%d')
    elif logdate == DateFormat.UNIX:
        authdate = now.strftime('%s')
    elif DateFormat.is_custom(logdate):
        fmt = DateFormat.get_custom_format(logdate)
        authdate = now.strftime(fmt)
    else:
        authdate = now.strftime('%c %z')
    return authdate

class GraphDelegate(QtWidgets.QStyledItemDelegate):
    LANE_WIDTH = 16
    DOT_RADIUS = 5
    EDGE_WIDTH = 3
    commit_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.white)
    merge_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.lightGray)
    head_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.green)
    current_head_color = QtGui.QColor(255, 215, 0)  # Gold color. Plain yellow is too close to white
    outline_pen = QtGui.QPen()
    outline_pen.setWidth(2)
    outline_pen.setColor(QtGui.QColor(Qt.white).darker())

    other_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.white)
    remote_color = QtGui.QColor(Qt.yellow)

    text_pen = QtGui.QPen()
    text_pen.setColor(QtGui.QColor(Qt.black))
    text_pen.setWidth(1)

    head_pen = QtGui.QPen()
    head_pen.setColor(QtGui.QColor(Qt.black))
    head_pen.setWidth(1)

    LABEL_BORDER = 3
    LABEL_SPACING = 4
    LABEL_TEXT_OFFSET = 3

    @perf.time_method('GraphDelegate.paint')
    def paint(self, painter, option, index):
        row = index.data(GRAPH_ROW_ROLE)
        prev_row = index.data(GRAPH_PREV_ROW_ROLE)

        painter.save()
        painter.setRenderHint(QtGui.QPainter.Antialiasing)
        painter.setClipRect(option.rect)

        rect = option.rect
        mid_y = rect.center().y()
        top_y = rect.top()
        # +1 to connect to the next row (FlatCap ends lines exactly at the endpoint)
        bottom_y = rect.bottom() + 1
        lane_w = self.LANE_WIDTH

        if option.state & QtWidgets.QStyle.State_Selected:
            painter.fillRect(rect, option.palette.highlight())

        # Draw the graph if we have graph data.
        if row is not None or prev_row is not None:
            pen = QtGui.QPen()
            pen.setWidth(self.EDGE_WIDTH)
            pen.setCapStyle(Qt.FlatCap)

            # Top half: edges from the previous row arrive vertically.
            if prev_row is not None:
                for edge in prev_row.edges_to_parent:
                    color = EdgeColor.colors[edge.color_index % len(EdgeColor.colors)]
                    pen.setColor(color)
                    painter.setPen(pen)
                    to_x = rect.left() + edge.to_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                    painter.drawLine(to_x, top_y, to_x, mid_y)

            # Bottom half: straight or spline depending on diagonal.
            if row is not None:
                for edge in row.edges_to_parent:
                    color = EdgeColor.colors[edge.color_index % len(EdgeColor.colors)]
                    pen.setColor(color)
                    painter.setPen(pen)
                    from_x = rect.left() + edge.from_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                    to_x = rect.left() + edge.to_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                    if edge.from_column == edge.to_column:
                        painter.drawLine(from_x, mid_y, to_x, bottom_y)
                    else:
                        path = QtGui.QPainterPath()
                        path.moveTo(from_x, mid_y)
                        path.cubicTo(
                            from_x,
                            bottom_y,
                            to_x,
                            mid_y,
                            to_x,
                            bottom_y,
                        )
                        painter.drawPath(path)

            if row is not None:
                cx = rect.left() + row.commit_column * lane_w + lane_w // 2
                color_map = {
                    GraphRowColor.NORMAL: self.commit_color,
                    GraphRowColor.MERGE: self.merge_color,
                    GraphRowColor.HEAD: self.current_head_color,
                }
                painter.setPen(self.outline_pen)
                painter.setBrush(color_map[row.color])
                painter.drawEllipse(
                    QtCore.QPointF(cx, mid_y), self.DOT_RADIUS, self.DOT_RADIUS
                )

        commit = index.data(COMMIT_ROLE)

        label_x = rect.left() + self._graph_width(row, prev_row) + 8
        labels_width = 0

        if commit and commit.tags:
            painter.setFont(option.font)
            labels_width = self._draw_labels(
                painter, mid_y, commit.tags, label_x, option.fontMetrics
            )

        text = index.data(Qt.DisplayRole)
        if text:
            text_x = int(label_x + labels_width + 8)
            text_rect = rect.adjusted(text_x - rect.left(), 0, 0, 0)
            painter.setPen(option.palette.text().color())
            painter.drawText(
                text_rect,
                Qt.AlignLeft | Qt.AlignVCenter,
                text,
            )

        painter.restore()

    @perf.time_method('GraphDelegate._draw_labels')
    def _draw_labels(
        self,
        painter: Optional[QtGui.QPainter],
        y: int,
        tags: list[str],
        start_x: int,
        font_metrics: QtGui.QFontMetrics,
    ):
        """Draw branch/tag labels and return total width used."""
        HEAD = 'HEAD'
        remotes_prefix = 'remotes/'
        tags_prefix = 'tags/'
        heads_prefix = 'heads/'
        remotes_len = len(remotes_prefix)
        tags_len = len(tags_prefix)
        heads_len = len(heads_prefix)

        current_x = start_x
        x_offset = self.LABEL_TEXT_OFFSET
        y_offset = 0

        for tag in tags:
            if tag == HEAD:
                continue

            pen = self.text_pen
            brush = self.other_color
            display_tag = tag

            if tag.startswith(remotes_prefix):
                display_tag = tag[remotes_len:]
            elif tag.startswith(tags_prefix):
                display_tag = tag[tags_len:]
                brush = self.remote_color
            elif tag.startswith(heads_prefix):
                display_tag = tag[heads_len:]
                pen = self.head_pen
                brush = self.head_color

            if painter is not None:
                painter.setPen(pen)
                painter.setBrush(brush)

            # Calculate text width using font metrics for consistency
            text_width = font_metrics.horizontalAdvance(display_tag)
            text_height = font_metrics.height()

            text_rect = QtCore.QRectF(
                current_x, y - text_height / 2, text_width, text_height
            )

            box_rect = text_rect.adjusted(-x_offset, -y_offset, x_offset, y_offset)

            if painter is not None:
                painter.drawRoundedRect(box_rect, self.LABEL_BORDER, self.LABEL_BORDER)
                painter.drawText(text_rect, Qt.AlignCenter, display_tag)

            current_x += text_width + x_offset * 2 + self.LABEL_SPACING

        return current_x - start_x

    @perf.time_method('GraphDelegate._labels_width')
    def _labels_width(self, font_metrics: QtGui.QFontMetrics, tags: list[str]):
        """Calculate total width needed for all labels."""
        return self._draw_labels(None, 0, tags, 0, font_metrics)

    @perf.time_method('GraphDelegate._graph_width')
    def _graph_width(self, row, prev_row):
        """Calculate the width needed for the graph."""
        if row is None and prev_row is None:
            return 0
        max_col = 0

def _branch_tip_basenames(context, oid):
    """Return de-duplicated basenames of files **changed by** the commit
    at ``oid`` (vs. its first parent, falling back to the empty tree for
    root commits) whose relative paths do not start with an underscore.

    Used to build a "Rename to" suggestion that tags a branch with the
    work introduced by its tip commit.

    Returns ``[]`` when no eligible files are found, in which case the
    caller hides the "Rename to" menu entry entirely.
    """
    if not oid:
        return []
    try:
        paths = gitcmds.changed_files(context, oid)
    except Exception:
        return []
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for path in paths:
        if not path or path.startswith('_'):
            continue
        name = path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
        if name and name not in seen:
            seen.add(name)
            out.append(name)
    return out


def _agent_branch_part(name):
    """Return the agent name segment for branches starting with "agent_" or "agent/".

    The returned segment is the text after the prefix up to (but not including) the
    next "/" or ".", or the rest of the string when neither is present. Branches
    renamed from the DAG are named ``agent/{session id}.{file names}``, so "." must
    stop the segment as well in order to yield the bare session id. Returns None if
    name does not start with one of the recognized agent prefixes.

    >>> _agent_branch_part('agent/23ecce3c-dc37.SQALE_Quality_Model,notes.md')
    '23ecce3c-dc37'
    >>> _agent_branch_part('agent/23ecce3c-dc37/SQALE_Quality_Model')
    '23ecce3c-dc37'
    >>> _agent_branch_part('agent_23ecce3c-dc37')
    '23ecce3c-dc37'
    >>> _agent_branch_part('feature/agent/23ecce3c-dc37') is None
    True
    """
    for prefix in ('agent_', 'agent/'):
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            tail = name[len(prefix):]
            for separator in ('/', '.'):
                tail = tail.split(separator, 1)[0]
            return tail
    return None


def _split_remote_ref(name, remotes):
    """Split a remote-tracking label such as "origin/agent/x" into (remote, branch).

    ``remotes`` holds the configured remote names; the longest match wins so that
    remotes sharing a prefix resolve to the right one. Returns ``(None, None)``
    when no configured remote matches or when the label is a symbolic ``HEAD``,
    which is not a branch that can be deleted.

    >>> _split_remote_ref('origin/agent/23ecce3c', ['origin'])
    ('origin', 'agent/23ecce3c')
    >>> _split_remote_ref('origin/mirror/topic', ['origin', 'origin/mirror'])
    ('origin/mirror', 'topic')
    >>> _split_remote_ref('origin/HEAD', ['origin'])
    (None, None)
    >>> _split_remote_ref('upstream/main', ['origin'])
    (None, None)
    """
    for remote in sorted(remotes, key=len, reverse=True):
        prefix = remote + '/'
        if name.startswith(prefix):
            branch = name[len(prefix):]
            if not branch or branch == 'HEAD':
                return (None, None)
            return (remote, branch)
    return (None, None)


def _parse_branch_menu_env():
    """Parse ``$BRANCH_MENU`` into a list of ``(label, rel_path)`` tuples.

    Format: colon-separated entries, each ``Label>relative/path``. Example::

        BRANCH_MENU="Stop>_traj/stop.md:Memo>_traj/memo.md"
    """
    raw = core.getenv('BRANCH_MENU', '') or ''
    entries = []
    for chunk in raw.split(':'):
        chunk = chunk.strip()
        if not chunk or '>' not in chunk:
            continue
        label, _sep, path = chunk.partition('>')
        label = label.strip()
        path = path.strip()
        if label and path:
            entries.append((label, path))
    return entries

def _branch_tip_basenames(context, oid):
    """Return de-duplicated basenames of files **changed by** the commit
    at ``oid`` (vs. its first parent, falling back to the empty tree for
    root commits) whose relative paths do not start with an underscore.

    Used to build a "Rename to" suggestion that tags a branch with the
    work introduced by its tip commit.

    Returns ``[]`` when no eligible files are found, in which case the
    caller hides the "Rename to" menu entry entirely.
    """
    if not oid:
        return []
    try:
        paths = gitcmds.changed_files(context, oid)
    except Exception:
        return []
    seen = set()
    out = []
    for path in paths:
        if not path or path.startswith('_'):
            continue
        name = path.rsplit('/', 1)[-1]
        if name and name not in seen:
            seen.add(name)
            out.append(name)
    return out

        ref = get(self.revtext)
        count = get(self.maxresults)
        context = self.context
        model = self.model
        display_status = get(self.display_status_action)
        # The DAG tries to avoid updating when the object IDs have not
        # changed.  Without doing this the DAG constantly redraws itself
        # whenever inotify sends update events, which hurts usability.
        #
        # To minimize redraws we leverage `git rev-parse`.  The strategy is to
        # use `git rev-parse` on the input line, which converts each argument
        # into object IDs.  From there it's a simple matter of detecting when
        # the object IDs changed.
        #
        # In addition to object IDs, we also need to know when the set of
        # named references (branches, tags) changes so that an update is
